<thought>From the observed mass spectrum we see a series of peaks spaced by ~1 Da with intensities that drop rapidly (100 → 14 → 1 → 0.07 → ...). This pattern is characteristic of the natural isotopic envelope of carbon atoms in a molecule (the M+1 peak from ¹³C grows with the number of carbons, producing a multi‑peak distribution). No distinctive M+2 pattern (e.g., ~1/3 for Cl or ~1 for Br) is present, so chlorine or bromine cannot be definitively identified. Therefore, the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution is carbon. 

<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
